compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: A800 has strong tensor-core throughput and large HBM bandwidth, but arbitrary-length FFTs and strict FP32 error tolerance complicate a pure-Triton implementation. Fixed widths 256, 768, 1024, and 64 are favorable for specialization.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Dense projections dominate arithmetic per token, while the Hyena convolution introduces an independent spectral or quadratic component. A mixed multi-kernel design is more realistic than literal whole-graph fusion.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: TF32 tensor-core accumulation may violate the tight end-to-end tolerance, while strict IEEE FP32 may leave substantial A800 throughput unused.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Intermediate tensors of sizes BLx768, Bx768xL, BLx1024, FFT workspaces, and repeated BLx256 residuals can dominate traffic unless adjacent pointwise operations are fused.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Materializing every reference intermediate can make moderate and long sequences bandwidth- and allocation-heavy despite compute-dense GEMMs.

register_pressure.notes: LayerNorm width 256 is manageable per row, but fusing projection, convolution, gating, or MLP tiles would rapidly increase accumulator and live-value counts.
register_pressure.risk: Over-fusion can reduce occupancy or spill, especially for 768- and 1024-wide projections.

nodes.notes:
1) Classification: mixed dense matrix multiplication, row reductions, depthwise causal stencil, generated-filter MLP, long 1-D convolution, gating, and pointwise residual/GELU work. Output is dense [B,L,256]. Reductions occur over model/inner dimensions, LayerNorm width 256, and convolution time. Access is dense and regular. Fixed dimensions are D=256, inner projection width=768, MLP width=1024, filter width=64, embedding width=5, and short kernel=3; B and L are runtime variables, with Lf=min(L,32768).
2) Canonical math: LN1(X) feeds U=LN1(X)Win^T+bin; each of 768 channels receives a causal three-tap cross-correlation, then Uc splits as x0,x1,v. A length-Lf positional feature z(t) passes through 5->64->64->64->256 sinusoidal layers and exponential modulation to form k. The Hyena core is q=v*x1, c=causal_conv(q,k)+q*filter_bias, y=x0*c. Then R=X+linear(y), and O=R+linear2(GELU(linear1(LN2(R)))). Rows, channels, and batches are independently parallel except for LayerNorm reductions, GEMM reductions, filter generation, and time convolution. Filter generation is batch-independent and reusable. For L>32768, LN1/input projection on the tail are dead; the Hyena tail is zero before output projection, so only out-projection bias, residual, LN2, and MLP remain. Stable FP32 reduction and exact FFT normalization are correctness-critical.
3) Layout: activations and weights begin contiguous FP32. Hidden/output are token-major [B,L,256]. The projected [B,L,768] is logically transposed to [B,768,L] for depthwise convolution and FFT gating, creating a layout conflict with GEMMs. Weight matrices are row-major and reused across all BL rows. The generated filter [L,256] is shared across B. Small normalization vectors and short-convolution coefficients can reside in registers/cache; filter-MLP weights fit cache; tiled GEMM operands can use shared memory. Full projected activations, MLP expansion, and FFT workspace should not remain simultaneously materialized.
4) Regimes: (a) tiny BL or L below roughly tens of tokens: launch latency, weight reads, and LayerNorm overhead dominate; direct time convolution is plausible. (b) moderate L and BL: 256x768 and 256x1024 dense projections dominate and should map efficiently to A800 matrix hardware; intermediate traffic becomes secondary. (c) long L up to 32768: batched 256-channel convolution and FFT workspace/transpose traffic become important, with arbitrary 2L transform sizes and synchronization as major risks. (d) L>32768: Hyena work is capped, and tail MLP/residual compute dominates; dead-tail elimination is valuable. Large B increases reuse of the shared filter but multiplies activation FFTs.
5) Knobs: execution-family dispatch by L/B; token and output-feature tiling; FP32 versus TF32 dot precision; staged versus fused residual/LN/projection boundaries; token-major versus channel-major intermediates; direct versus spectral convolution; transform factorization for supported lengths; recomputation versus storage of generated filters; batch/channel grouping; dead-tail specialization; masked boundary handling; and GELU approximation matching.
6) Skeleton: generate the shared modulated filter once; compute LN1 and input projection in token tiles; apply the three-tap causal depthwise operation and split/gate; perform either direct or spectral causal convolution; apply final gate and output projection while adding the first residual; compute LN2; run 256->1024 GELU->256 and add the final residual. Synchronization is local to reductions/GEMM tiles, except spectral transforms require multiple global stages. Registers hold row statistics, short coefficients, gates, and small fragments; shared memory holds matrix or transform tiles.
7) Pruned families: staged universal execution is the lowest correctness risk and exposes phase timings but writes intermediates; a short-sequence direct Hyena path avoids FFT setup at quadratic cost; a long-sequence spectral Hyena path has the right asymptotic behavior but is hardest in pure Triton and sensitive to arbitrary lengths and normalization.

kernel_summary: This is a mixed end-to-end sequence block combining two width-256 LayerNorm reductions, three major dense projection groups, a 768-channel three-tap causal depthwise stencil, a batch-independent sinusoidal 5-to-64-to-64-to-64-to-256 filter generator, a gated 256-channel long causal convolution, GELU, and residual additions. Dense projections contribute roughly 1.57 million FLOPs per processed token and should fit A800 matrix hardware well, while short shapes are likely launch/weight-latency limited and long shapes may be dominated by FFT workspace, synchronization, and token-major versus channel-major layout traffic. The primary constraints are FP32 input/output with tight accumulated error tolerance, exact FFT scaling and causal cropping, fixed favorable widths, runtime B and L, Lf=min(L,32768), and the opportunity to eliminate dead LN1/Hyena projection work beyond Lf.
